title: Auto-rollback audit log UI mock notes (Console) — timeline + “why” panel + admin controls
content:
Context / what this doc is
Working UI notes for how Console should display auto actions (auto-pause, auto-rollback, suppressed) triggered by SLO breach evaluation during rollouts. This is not a pixel-perfect spec; it’s intended to align Console + controller + SRE on: (1) timeline UX, (2) “why did we rollback” explanation, (3) dashboard linking, and (4) admin-only controls.

Primary user goals
- On-call / SRE: quickly answer “what happened”, “is it still happening”, “was the rollback justified”, “is monitoring missing/stale”, “who/what initiated the action”, and “what do we do next”.
- Service/route owner: understand if regression correlates to a rollout step/model version/region and whether it impacted customer tier(s).
- Admin/platform operator: be able to suppress auto actions (temporary) with a justification that is auditable.

Where this UI lives (proposal)
1) Rollout detail page → new tab/section: “Timeline” (existing) extended with “Auto actions” events.
2) “Audit log” (global) → filterable stream that includes rollout auto actions (useful when starting from an alert/Slack message and you only have rollout_id).

High-level UX structure
A) Timeline (left column, main): ordered events with icons + compact summary.
B) Detail panel (right drawer): when you click an event, show full explanation + links.
C) Admin controls (top/right of detail panel): visible only to admins (RBAC), with justification capture.

Timeline view — event types & grouping
We should treat “auto action decision” as a first-class event, separate from “rollout step changed”. A single decision event can have multiple monitors/signals attached.

Event types to render (MVP)
- Auto-pause triggered
- Auto-rollback triggered
- Auto action suppressed (explicit suppression window or override)
- Rollback failed / executor error (if controller emits this)
- Monitor missing / stale (decision not possible, or fail-open behavior noted)

Grouping
- Prefer chronological list; don’t nest within step-change events (too easy to miss).
- But show “rollout step context” as a small chip: e.g., Step 3/7 → 10% canary → model v2026.02.14.
- If multiple decisions fire in a short period, show each but collapse visually (e.g., “3 decisions in 8m” with expand) to avoid noisy timelines.

Timeline row content (compact)
Row should answer “what action, where, when, who/what, and a 1-line why”.
- Icon: pause / rollback arrow / shield (suppressed) / warning (missing monitor) / red x (action failed)
- Title examples:
  - “Auto-rollback executed”
  - “Auto-pause executed”
  - “Auto-rollback suppressed”
  - “Auto-rollback attempted (failed)”
- Subtitle (1 line): “p99 latency burn-rate fast window breached (5m) + slow window breached (30m) — us-east-1 — tier: dedicated”
- Timestamp (absolute + relative)
- Actor: “rollout-controller” (system) OR “admin override: <name>” (if manual)

Detail panel — information architecture
Top summary (always visible)
- Status badge: Executed / Suppressed / Failed / No-op
- Action: Pause / Rollback / Shift traffic to baseline
- Scope: service/route, model version, region, customer tier, rollout_id
- Correlation IDs (copy buttons): rollout_id, decision_id, audit_event_id, trace_id (if present)

“Why did this happen?” section (core)
This should be a human-readable explanation constructed from structured fields, not free text.
Proposed template:
- “The rollout controller evaluated the rollout safety policy v<policy_version> for <scope>. It detected an SLO breach meeting rollback criteria (fast burn + slow burn) and executed <action>.”

Then show the evaluation factors as bullets:
- Signals evaluated:
  - Latency p99: breached (fast window 5m, burn-rate 14.2x) and breached (slow window 30m, burn-rate 3.1x)
  - Error rate: not breached
  - Saturation: not evaluated (not configured)
- Minimum sample gate:
  - “Requests observed: 18,240 (min required: 5,000) → gate passed”
  - If not passed, we must show: “Gate failed: insufficient volume → action suppressed/no-op”
- Debounce / holdoff:
  - “Debounce: 2 consecutive evaluations required → satisfied”
  - “Holdoff: 10m between actions → not applicable / satisfied”
- Suppression checks:
  - “No suppression window active” OR “Suppressed due to active override ‘Telemetry incident’ until 2026-02-18 15:30 UTC”

Show “Decision trace” (collapsed by default)
- A structured list of the decision steps (think: decision tree) for auditability.
- Example:
  1. Evaluate monitors for scope
  2. Validate monitor freshness
  3. Check min sample
  4. Compute burn-rate thresholds
  5. Apply debounce/holdoff
  6. Check suppression
  7. Choose action (pause vs rollback)
  8. Execute via rollback executor

Metrics snapshot (don’t overdo it)
We should not re-implement Grafana. Instead show:
- A small “sparkline-like” mini chart is optional later; MVP: show numeric snapshot at decision time.
- Fields:
  - p95 latency, p99 latency (ms)
  - error rate (%), 5xx rate (%), timeout rate (%)
  - request volume (req/min)
  - evaluation windows (fast/slow)
  - monitor timestamps (last data time)

If monitor data is missing/stale
We need a clear, non-blamey explanation + what to do.
- Banner: “Monitor data missing or stale — auto actions may be suppressed.”
- Show:
  - Which monitor ID(s) were queried
  - Last successful datapoint time
  - Staleness threshold
  - Controller behavior: fail-open vs fail-closed (we should mirror the actual policy; if we fail-open, say so explicitly)
- CTA: “Open monitor coverage checklist” (link to SRE doc / internal sheet), and “Contact #eng-sre” or the owning team.

Links (high value)
In the detail panel, always provide:
- “Open rollout health dashboard” (Grafana) → pre-filtered by rollout_id, service/route, region, tier
- “Open SLO detail dashboard” → pre-filtered by monitor id
- “View policy configuration” → link to policy editor (read-only snapshot at that policy_version)
- “View raw audit event JSON” (admin-only?)
- “Open related deploy / model version diff” (if we have model version + git sha or artifact link)

Link formatting note
Links need to work even when user is coming from Slack incident-bot message. So we should ensure the deep links can be constructed from rollout_id alone, and server-side can resolve missing context.

Admin-only controls (RBAC + audit)
Controls should be discoverable but gated.

Admin actions (MVP)
1) “Suppress auto actions…”
   - Scope: (a) this rollout only, (b) this service/route + region + tier (broader)
   - Duration: dropdown (30m, 2h, 6h, 24h) + custom
   - Reason (required): free text + optional incident link
   - Confirm modal: show what will be suppressed and expiration time
   - Result: create an audit event “suppression_set” with actor, reason, expiration

2) “Remove suppression”
   - Requires reason
   - Also emits audit event

3) “Mark as known incident (mute decisioning)” — NOT MVP?
   - Might overlap with suppression window. Keep as future if we want a more structured incident integration.

RBAC expectations
- Default: view timeline + detail panel for any user with rollout read access.
- Admin actions: only users with “rollout:auto_action_override” permission (see INT-8832 request).
- The UI should show a disabled control with tooltip “Admin permission required” so users know the feature exists.

Copy requirements (language)
Avoid implying certainty when data is partial.
Good:
- “The controller detected…”
- “Based on the configured policy…”
- “Monitor data was stale; actions were suppressed…”
Bad:
- “The model is broken.”
- “Rollback fixed it.”

Edge cases to handle
- Rollback executed but rollout later continues due to manual intervention → show both events (system rollback + manual resume).
- Multiple regions: a rollback may be region-scoped; timeline row must show region chip(s).
- A/B tests: action might be “shift traffic back to baseline” vs “rollback model version”. UI should generalize around “traffic policy change executed” with a subtype label.
- Rollback fails (executor error): show error code + retry semantics (idempotency); provide “View executor logs” link (internal).
- Oscillation prevention: if holdoff prevents repeated actions, show “Suppressed by holdoff (10m)” rather than “No action”.
- Pagination: audit timelines can get long; ensure stable sort by server-provided event_time + event_id.

Data dependencies (what Console needs)
Minimum fields needed to render MVP well (align with ADR-0128 + API work):
- event_type (auto_pause|auto_rollback|suppressed|failed|missing_monitor)
- event_time
- rollout_id
- scope fields: service, route, model_version, region, customer_tier
- action fields: action_taken, action_target (e.g., reverted_to_model_version), rollout_step
- evaluation summary:
  - signals list + per-signal status
  - burn-rate windows + thresholds
  - sample size + min required
  - debounce/holdoff outcomes
  - suppression reason (if any)
- monitor references: monitor_ids, last_data_ts, staleness_status
- actor: system vs admin user id + display name
- policy_version
- links: dashboard urls (optional; if absent we can generate based on conventions)

Open questions / decisions to make
- Do we show raw monitor query outputs anywhere? (My preference: no by default; expose behind “raw JSON” link for admins.)
- Fail-open vs fail-closed messaging: need final decision from SRE + controller behavior; UI must reflect actual semantics.
- Should “suppressed” events appear in timeline by default? For SRE yes (it explains why no rollback happened). For general users, maybe behind a toggle. Proposal: show by default but with low-contrast styling.
- Should we show a “recommended next step” section? (E.g., “Investigate recent change in batching config”). Might be too opinionated for MVP.

Next steps (for DES-944 / ENG-4833)
- Alicia/Kenji: turn this into a simple wireframe for the detail panel + timeline row states (executed/suppressed/failed/missing).
- Felix/Chloe: confirm API payload shape supports “why” template without new backend work; identify any missing fields.
- Rafael: review for on-call usability; confirm which fields reduce time-to-triage.
- Validate with one game day scenario: show a timeline with (1) monitor stale warning, (2) later auto-pause, (3) then auto-rollback after slow burn confirmed, and ensure the UI tells a coherent story.

Notes from quick review (2026-02-20)
- Strong preference from SRE: keep “monitor missing/stale” highly visible; past incidents failed because people assumed auto rollback would trigger.
- Also: avoid auto-paging storms; the UI should reflect when multiple decisions were suppressed by holdoff (so on-call doesn’t think the system is thrashing).
